# Concepts Model

The Concepts Model fixes the vocabulary: concepts, their attributes and their relations (`isa`, part-of, and plain relations with a label and a multiplicity).

Method: 4EM (Sandkuhl, Stirna, Persson and Wißotzki, *Enterprise Modeling: Tackling Business Challenges with the 4EM Method*, Springer 2014). Every element cites its source; `decided` means a source shows that the operator decided it.

| <a id="concept-org-ir"></a><code>concept-org-ir</code><br/>Concept | **Persistent IR.** The intermediate representation of a story: JSON owned by reebeat, with a schema for a chosen subset of SMIL, SCXML and FRP constructs. It is a format authors and tools edit, not an artifact. Attributes: a schema for a chosen subset of SMIL, SCXML and FRP constructs; isomorphic codecs where formats round-trip. | decided |  | [log L25][1] |
| <a id="concept-org-artifact"></a><code>concept-org-artifact</code><br/>Concept | **Artifact.** A produced file or site that people consume: a video, a presentation deck, or an interactive website. Artifact formats are not IR formats. Fountain is both an importer (a screenplay becomes a story) and an artifact renderer (a story becomes a screenplay); it is not the persistent IR, which stays JSON. Attributes: static or dynamic interface; interaction surfaces. | decided |  | [log L25][1], [log L37][2], [log L67-69][3] |
| <a id="concept-org-interaction"></a><code>concept-org-interaction</code><br/>Concept | **Interaction.** An interaction is an element that can trigger events. | <a id="concept-org-tier"></a><code>concept-org-tier</code><br/>Concept | **Free and paid tier.** A free tier holds the basic features that cost nothing to run. | <a id="concept-org-agent-tool-protocol"></a><code>concept-org-agent-tool-protocol</code><br/>Concept | **Agent tool protocol.** Each tool through which an agent reads a story, applies an edit and runs the checks is declared once, in a protocol-neutral way.     concept_studio_repair_proposal --> concept_studio_validation_gate : offered after a refusal
    concept_studio_suggestion --> concept_studio_json_patch : applies as
    concept_studio_suggestion --> concept_studio_repair_proposal : a repair is one kind
    concept_studio_sync_room --> concept_studio_keyed_document : holds the shared copy of
    concept_studio_peer --> concept_studio_loro_update : produces
    concept_studio_lens <|-- concept_studio_deck_view
    concept_studio_deck_view *-- concept_studio_take
    concept_studio_deck_view *-- concept_studio_narration_piece
    concept_studio_anchor_offset --> concept_studio_narration_piece : an anchor can be a narration word
    concept_studio_agent_scope --> concept_studio_suggestion : suggest scope creates

| <a id="concept-flow-attribution"></a><code>concept-flow-attribution</code><br/>Concept | **Attribution.** Attribution is the "Built with xyflow" link in the corner of the canvas. It is either Visible or Hidden. Visible is the default, and an application may set it to Hidden. Attributes: Visible or Hidden; link to xyflow.com. | decided |  | [log L106][77], [foldkit-flow:README.md:86][78], [foldkit-flow:docs/specs/0000-development-lifecycle.md:53][79], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/attribution.ts:15-22][80] |
| <a id="concept-flow-out-message"></a><code>concept-flow-out-message</code><br/>Concept | **Out-message (outcome).** An out-message tells the application what a gesture produced: Connected, Reconnected, Deleted, Moved or a selection change. The library only reports it, and the application decides what to do with it and applies the graph change. | decided |  | [log L109][81], [foldkit-flow:README.md:52][82], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/message.ts:67-83][83] |
| <a id="concept-flow-flow"></a><code>concept-flow-flow</code><br/>Concept | **Flow.** A Flow is one node-based graph canvas inside a Foldkit application. It holds the nodes, edges, viewport and selection, and it lives in the application's Model. Attributes: id; nodes; edges; viewport; attribution option. *Why proposed:* The log decides only a node-based graph UI for Foldkit (line 48). README line 24 says the Flow is a Foldkit Submodel whose graph lives in the application's Model, and model.ts lines 14 to 29 define its fields: nodes, edges, viewport and attribution. Selection is a flag on each node and edge. The operator must confirm the concept. | proposed |  | [log L48][84], [foldkit-flow:README.md:3][85], [foldkit-flow:README.md:24][86], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/model.ts:14-29][87] |
| <a id="concept-flow-node"></a><code>concept-flow-node</code><br/>Concept | **Node.** A node is one box on the canvas. It declares its position, size and handles, and the application draws its content. Attributes: id; label; type; position; width and height; handles; parent id; clamped to parent. *Why proposed:* README lines 35 to 47 show the node fields in use, and types.ts lines 42 to 59 define them. A node declares its size and handles, so edges are placed without measuring the DOM. The operator must confirm the vocabulary. | proposed |  | [foldkit-flow:README.md:3][85], [foldkit-flow:README.md:35-47][88], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/types.ts:42-59][89] |
| <a id="concept-flow-edge"></a><code>concept-flow-edge</code><br/>Concept | **Edge.** An edge is a line between a source handle and a target handle. It can be a bezier, smooth-step or straight line, with an optional arrow. Attributes: id; source node and handle; target node and handle; kind; arrow; label. *Why proposed:* README line 47 shows an edge, and line 66 says there are three edge types with an optional arrow. types.ts lines 63 to 77 define the kinds (Bezier, SmoothStep, Straight) and the fields, including a label. The operator must confirm the vocabulary. | proposed |  | [foldkit-flow:README.md:47][90], [foldkit-flow:README.md:66][91], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/types.ts:63-77][92] |
| <a id="concept-flow-handle"></a><code>concept-flow-handle</code><br/>Concept | **Handle.** A handle is a connection point on a node. A person drags from one handle to another to make a connection. Attributes: id; kind (source or target); side. *Why proposed:* The README names handles (line 3) and shows one declared on a node (line 43). types.ts lines 33 to 38 define a handle by id, kind (source or target) and side. The operator must confirm the vocabulary. | proposed |  | [foldkit-flow:README.md:3][85], [foldkit-flow:README.md:43][93], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/types.ts:33-38][94] |
| <a id="concept-flow-connection"></a><code>concept-flow-connection</code><br/>Concept | **Connection.** A connection is a pair of handles that a person joins with a gesture. The application's check accepts or refuses it, and the application turns an accepted one into an edge. *Why proposed:* types.ts lines 81 to 89 define a connection as the two ends of an edge that is about to exist. README lines 53 and 54 say the application adds the edge when it receives `Connected`. So a connection (a gesture result) differs from an edge (graph data). The operator must confirm. | proposed |  | [foldkit-flow:README.md:53-54][95], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/types.ts:81-89][96] |
| <a id="concept-flow-parent-node"></a><code>concept-flow-parent-node</code><br/>Concept | **Compound (parent) node.** A parent node contains child nodes. A child positions relative to its parent and may be clamped inside it. A Scene holding States is one example. Attributes: children; clamp to parent. *Why proposed:* The log says a Scene is a compound state that groups States (line 19). The library builds parent nodes for that shape: a node with `parentId` is a child whose position is relative to its parent (README line 45), and `isClampedToParent` keeps it inside (README line 66; types.ts line 52). No line names the node kind as a flow concept. The operator must confirm. | proposed |  | [log L19][13], [foldkit-flow:README.md:45][97], [foldkit-flow:README.md:66][91], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/types.ts:52-54][98] |
| <a id="concept-flow-viewport"></a><code>concept-flow-viewport</code><br/>Concept | **Viewport.** The viewport is the visible part of the canvas, given by an offset and a zoom. Pan and zoom change it and touch no node. Attributes: x offset; y offset; zoom. *Why proposed:* The README names pan and zoom (line 3) and says they change only the viewport element's transform (line 82). types.ts lines 10 to 14 define the viewport as x, y and zoom, and model.ts line 28 holds it in the Model. The operator must confirm. | proposed |  | [foldkit-flow:README.md:3][85], [foldkit-flow:README.md:82][99], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/types.ts:10-14][100] |
| <a id="concept-flow-selection"></a><code>concept-flow-selection</code><br/>Concept | **Selection.** The selection is the set of nodes and edges the person has picked by click, box or key. Delete, move and clear act on it. *Why proposed:* The README names selecting with a box (line 3) and lists click, Shift-click and box selection (line 66). Selection is a `selected` flag on each node and edge (selection.ts lines 5 to 7), and `UpdatedSelection` reports it (message.ts line 79). The operator must confirm. | proposed |  | [foldkit-flow:README.md:3][85], [foldkit-flow:README.md:66][91], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/selection.ts:5-7][101] |
| <a id="concept-flow-minimap"></a><code>concept-flow-minimap</code><br/>Concept | **Minimap and controls.** The minimap is a small overview of the graph that a person can drag to pan. The controls are buttons to zoom in, zoom out and fit the view. *Why proposed:* README line 66 lists a minimap, zoom controls and fit view as built. view.ts draws the controls (lines 464 to 478) and the minimap (lines 499 to 523), and the minimap Mount lets a person drag it to pan (mounts.ts lines 757 to 779). The operator must confirm them as part of the first release. | proposed |  | [foldkit-flow:README.md:66][91], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/view.ts:464-478][102], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/view.ts:499-523][103] |
| <a id="concept-flow-mount"></a><code>concept-flow-mount</code><br/>Concept | **Mount.** A Mount is a Foldkit construct that runs work when an element appears and cleans up when it goes. The library uses Mounts to own its controllers. *Why proposed:* Mount is a Foldkit term, used here as AGENTS.md uses it. mounts.ts lines 34 to 39 say each xyflow controller is created and destroyed by a Mount. The operator must confirm that it belongs in the model. | proposed |  | [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:63][104], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/mounts.ts:34-39][105] |
| <a id="concept-flow-controller"></a><code>concept-flow-controller</code><br/>Concept | **Controller.** A controller is an xyflow object that handles one kind of interaction: pan and zoom, node drag, handle connection or the minimap. *Why proposed:* The README lists xyflow's controllers (line 86). xyflow.ts lines 7 to 20 name the four the library calls: XYPanZoom, XYDrag, XYMinimap and the handle gesture XYHandle.onPointerDown. The operator must confirm. | proposed |  | [foldkit-flow:README.md:86][78], [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:63][104], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/xyflow.ts:7-20][106] |
| <a id="concept-flow-live-region"></a><code>concept-flow-live-region</code><br/>Concept | **Live region.** The live region is a polite status area that announces selection, moves, connections and deletions to screen readers. *Why proposed:* README line 76 says a polite live region (`role="status"`) announces selection, moves, connections and deletions, and view.ts lines 665 to 673 render it. The operator must confirm the live region as part of the keyboard contract. | proposed |  | [foldkit-flow:README.md:76][107], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/view.ts:665-673][108] |
